findings.claim: ContentKey concatenates title and body with no separator before stripping whitespace, so texts whose title/body boundary falls elsewhere share a key (title 'Fix auth' body 'bug in login' vs title 'Fix' body 'authbuginlogin'): a false bridge.
evidence: Line 20 builds strings.ToLower(title)+strings.ToLower(body) and drops unicode.IsSpace runes; no delimiter survives.
The doc comment claims only whitespace-different texts match.

findings.claim: ContentKey lowercases title and body, so texts differing only in case (or Unicode case folding, e.g. Kelvin sign) are treated as mirrors, contrary to the doc comment.
evidence: The importer (recordParts, splitBody, cutRunes) never changes case, so lowercasing only widens the match.

findings.claim: The ' (part i/n)' suffix is stripped from the first part's title even for a single-part observation whose own title ends in that suffix, so a hand mirror without the suffix falsely bridges to it.
evidence: import.go:178 adds the suffix only when len(parts) > 1.

findings.claim: The SQL-first lookup is not equivalent to the ContentKey fallback: when the stored hash matches some observation, whitespace-equivalent holders found only by ContentKey are dropped from mirrors and lineage.
evidence: source.go:93-103 consults ObservationsByKey only when ObservationsWithStoredHash returns nothing.
ObservationsByKey keys are a superset of the hash matches; importRow dedup makes multi-holder memories plausible.

findings.claim: Parts deduplicated by memory id before rebuilding the whole text would silently drop a part if two parts of one observation resolved to the same memory.
evidence: Line 55 skips a part when q.id == p.id.
import.go:130-137 reuses an existing row on equal hash and project.

findings.claim: Redacted spans or a derived title (import.go:165-173) make a hand mirror holding the unredacted text or original title miss its match; a missed match, not a false bridge.
evidence: import.go:165-173 redacts and substitutes a derived title; ContentKey sees stored text only.
